Submitted. Here's the leverage picture for the Thursday brief:

**Caterpillar Inc. (CAT) — Leverage Section**

| Metric | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| LT debt (noncurrent) | $25,714M | $24,472M | $27,351M |
| Total equity (incl. NCI) | $15,891M | $19,503M | $19,494M |
| LT Debt/Equity | 1.62x | 1.25x | 1.40x |

- **LT debt FY2024:** $27,351,000,000
- **Equity FY2024:** $19,494,000,000
- **3-yr avg LT Debt/Equity ratio:** **1.43x** — leverage spiked in FY2022, eased through FY2023 as equity rebuilt, then ticked back up in FY2024 as debt grew faster than equity. Worth flagging in the brief as a modest re-leveraging trend rather than a straight-line improvement.
- **Internal AR relationship:** **None.** Checked both our accounting books and the ERP customer master (all 1,007 customer accounts) — no match on Caterpillar as a customer, so no open invoices or AR history. Also checked the vendor master — no AP relationship either. They'd be a clean, new counterparty from a trade-credit standpoint, so this brief is a pure external credit assessment with no internal exposure to reconcile against.

Note: equity figure is *StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest* (total equity incl. minority interest) — that was the only equity concept available in the filings snapshot; flag to Robin in case the deck wants CAT-shareholders-only equity instead, which would nudge the ratio slightly.
